en: The *Vajramahākālastotra* composed by Ācārya Nāgārjuna:
with the sounds of the syllables *hāṃ hāṃ hāṃ*, with shouts of *kilikilita*, and with hosts of *bhūtas* and *vetālas*...

May the Protector of the Field (Kṣetrapāla) protect you—he who utters "rhu" and "huṃ" on all sides; whose face is filled with human flesh; whose limbs are garlanded with blood; who holds a skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) and a severed hand; who carries a skull-bowl (narakara); who can assume any form at will; who is deformed; who has tawny eyes and tawny hair; and who wears a necklace of skeletons from the hosts of corpses. || 1 ||

With his mouth and limbs filled with the great fire produced by the sounds "pheṃ pheṃ pheṃ," placing a garland around his neck, his body manifesting fear yet adorned with ornaments; with slightly reddened lips and a hand released from the garland encircled by all the blood; pheṃ pheṃ pheṃkāranādaiḥ pratijanitabṛhadvahnigarbhāṅgavaktre mālāṃ kaṇṭhe nidhāya prakaṭabhayavapurbhūṣitāṅgopaśobhaḥ | īṣadraktādharoṣṭho'sṛkasakalavṛtāmālinā muktapāṇiḥ || 1 ||
May the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapa), with the sounds "klīṃ ḍāṃ klīṃ ḍāṃ" in the land of the excellent fire, protect you all. || 2 ||

KṢAṂ KṢAṂ KṢAṂ, the embodiment of forbearance, making the sound *kalakala-kala*, increasing patience; having traversed and pervaded the entire universe, uttering the sound *kahaka-haha*; the color of a dark blue cloud; HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ KLĪṂ, whose body is mantra; cook, cook with fires—the mantra born from all sides!
May Kṣetrapāla, who drives away obstacles, surely pacify our enemies. || 3 ||

Hā hā hā! With his loud, piercing laughter that always causes extreme terror to wicked beings and evil-doers, he—who has attained the realization of perfect awakening—is the destroyer of obstacles day by day. Filling the hollows of the three worlds with the sounds of "huṃ phaṭ huṃ phaṭ," he is possessed of full power.
May the illustrious Kṣetrapāla protect you—he whose body bears the weight of a mass of matted hair as tawny as a young monkey.
Khaṃ khaṃ khaṃ! With sword in hand, he is playful with the *lalala* sounds; in form, he has blood-red palms.

Raṃ raṃ raṃ! He has blood-red eyes; ru ru! He has hands smeared with blood and possesses fierce speed (*caṇḍavega*). Kruṃ kruṃ kruṃ! He has a gaze of wrath; kuha kuha! He is crooked and has completely crushed all that is wicked.
Ḍaṃ ḍaṃ ḍaṃ! May Kṣetrapāla, whose body is the ḍamaru drum and who is accompanied by his ḍamaru, protect us. || 5 ||

Whomever and whatever the universe reaches— whether by night or by day, whether disciplined or undisciplined— he moves with the speed of the wind, instantly holding a water-jar, having attained worldly honor;
with limbs terrifying by the syllables *bhrūṃ bhrūṃ bhrūṃ*, causing fear with his knitted brows, he bestows liberation upon practitioners.
Kṣaṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ! May the bringer of security, Kṣetrapāla, destroy all evil and protect us. || 6 ||
*klāṃ klāṃ klāṃ*, you who are the embodiment of movement, constantly moistening the three worlds;
*paṃ paṃ paṃ*, with noose in hand and axe held in your grasp, always protecting those worthy of protection;
you are the mantra-form of all mudrās, the bestower of desired fruits to practitioners, and equal to the mantras themselves.
May he, the protector of the fields, whose body has conquered all [senses], and who possesses long life, protect you for a long time. || 7 ||
Klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ! You who are clothed in a hide, you who have subdued your enemies, the refuge of those afflicted by suffering;
Kaṃ kaṃ kaṃ! You who wear a garland of skulls, the remover of the impurities of the Kali age, whose body is like a multitude of dark clouds;
Caṃ caṃ caṃ! You of fierce speed, whose conduct follows the established law, the sole world for those who have become Time itself.
May he, whose self is perfectly restrained, protect you—may he who observes the auspicious fruits of his vows grant his protection. || 8 ||
The body of mantras, possessing the fixed splendor of Yama, is the teacher or the practitioner on the pure bank of the true path; he who recites them regularly becomes meritorious,
and [attains] longevity, prosperity, fame, fortune, steadfastness, incomparable strength, peace, nourishment, and radiance.
And omniscience is eternal; day and night, the incomparable mass of obstacles is destroyed. || 9 ||
The *Śrīvajramahākālastotra* is completed.
